patch_description: Instead of LP-in-the-loop hill climbing (slow, limits steps to ~250), this version uses a fast iterative shrink solver for radii evaluation, enabling thousands of cheap local-search steps. Key novelty: hybrid "contact-gradient push" moves — each circle is nudged along the weighted average direction away from its touching neighbors and walls (a quasi-gradient of its own max radius), interleaved with random perturbations. Multi-start from several structured layouts (staggered hex rows with different counts) picks the best basin. A final LP polish (if scipy available) squeezes the last bit from the best center configuration. This gave large gains over the previous approach at similar runtime.
